bibliographic.title: Bridging the gap: a practical step-by-step approach to warrant safe implementation of large language models in healthcare
bibliographic.authors: Jessica D. Workum, Davy van de Sande, Diederik Gommers, Michel E. van Genderen
bibliographic.citation_apa: Workum, J. D., van de Sande, D., Gommers, D., & van Genderen, M. E. (2025). Bridging the gap: A practical step-by-step approach to warrant safe implementation of large language models in healthcare. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 8, 1504805. https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2025.1504805

methodology.method_family: perspective article with normative framework and step-by-step recommendations
methodology.sample_description: not applicable; no empirical sample described in provided text
methodology.technology_context: large language models for healthcare applications including administrative tasks and clinical decision support; medical domain adaptation via healthcare-specific models or knowledge integration

eligibility.decision_rationale: Peer-reviewed perspective explicitly addressing responsible and safe LLM implementation in healthcare, proposing actionable governance recommendations, structured output evaluation (ACUTE), and model governance structure. Strong alignment with LLM governance in regulated healthcare despite no conversational-AI focus in the provided excerpt.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial pages 1-2 were supplied; conversational-AI relevance cannot be confirmed from excerpt, and empirical validation of the proposed framework is not evidenced in the text provided.

appraisal.notes: Perspective/framework paper without empirical study design; recommendations are clearly articulated but not empirically tested in the provided text. Appropriate for conceptual contribution on safe LLM implementation governance in healthcare.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is internally coherent and highly relevant to regulated healthcare LLM governance, but confidence is moderated because the supplied text is partial, the article is non-empirical, and conversational-system governance is not evidenced.

coding.theme: Governance framework for safe LLM deployment in healthcare
coding.subtheme: Practical step-by-step implementation and response assessment
concepts: ACUTE (Accuracy, Consistency, semantically Unaltered outputs, Traceability, Ethical considerations)
rq_alignment: risk control and traceability in healthcare AI

synthesis.main_claim: The authors propose a practical step-by-step approach to support healthcare organizations in responsibly and safely implementing LLMs, including privacy protection, medical prompt engineering, CDS/non-CDS distinction, structured output evaluation, and model governance, plus the ACUTE mnemonic for assessing LLM responses.
synthesis.contribution: Provides actionable implementation guidance and an evaluation mnemonic (ACUTE) aimed at bridging the gap between LLM potential and clear organizational guidelines in healthcare.
synthesis.limitations: Perspective without empirical validation in the provided text; general-purpose LLM limitations for specialized healthcare tasks are acknowledged, but broader study limitations are not fully visible in the excerpt; no conversational-AI or chatbot-specific governance addressed in supplied pages.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as central conceptual evidence on operational and model governance for LLMs in regulated healthcare, especially for safe implementation pathways, output evaluation, traceability, and ethics; triangulate with conversational-governance studies because conversational systems are not explicitly covered in the excerpt.

evidence.claim: ACUTE framework covers traceability and ethical assessment of responses
